sharpened.demo_script:
0:00-0:25 — COLD OPEN. Screen shows 30 red donor-patient pairs clustered around 4 SF hospitals, all disconnected. "Ninety thousand Americans are waiting for a kidney. Every red pair on this screen is a patient whose husband, sister, or friend is ready to donate today — and can't, because the blood type is wrong. Each pair is a dead end. Until someone connects them."

0:25-0:55 — THE INTAKE. Presenter pastes a genuinely messy referral email ("...pt's neighbor Maria G, healthy 44F, O-neg, presented at UCSF wanting non-directed donation, cleared psych eval...") into the intake box. byLLM's parse_intake mints a typed AltruisticDonor node that drops into the UCSF cluster, gold. "No form. No schema. One paragraph became a typed node in a persistent graph — that's one line of Jac."

0:55-1:35 — THE CHAIN. Click FIND CHAINS. Compatibility edges fade in, then the ChainSeeker walker animates hop by hop — Maria's kidney to Patient 3, Pair 3's donor to Patient 11, onward — six hops across three hospitals flash gold. Lives counter ticks 0 to 6. Plain-English narration scrolls: "Maria gives to David at UCSF; David's wife Ana gives to..." — "The walker's carried state IS the chain. This is the same class of algorithm UNOS actually runs, on the domain that invented it."

1:35-2:20 — THE CONFLICT. Two rival chains light up, both needing Pair 12 — approving one kills the other. Three hospital advocate agents file arguments on screen, each openly biased toward its own patients. The written ethics policy is visible in the sidebar. The arbiter rules: approves the 6-chain and a 3-cycle, rejects the rival, with a written rationale citing policy rule 2. Counter ticks to 9. "The LLM reasons; Jac enforces the invariants — the ruling is machine-verified disjoint before anything executes."

2:20-3:20 — THE GUT PUNCH (the wow moment setup). Presenter clicks "Donor 7 has withdrawn." The 6-chain shatters gray on screen, counter flashes 9 down to 3, three stranded patients pulse red. Beat of silence. "In the real world this happens constantly, and stranded patients go back to the end of the line." Then — unprompted — the DropoutWalker re-plans: the ChainSeeker re-spawns from the stranded pairs and a rescue chain relights node by node across the hospitals. Counter climbs to 7. "Nobody clicked anything. The system detected the break, re-planned, and saved four of the six on its own."

3:20-4:00 — THE CLOSE + PERSISTENCE FLEX. Presenter kills the Jac process in the terminal, restarts it — graph, chains, and counter are all still there. "Zero database code. This entire system — the graph, the matching algorithm, four kinds of agents — is about 500 lines of Jac." Final frame: the lives counter, large: 7. "Seven people who were dead ends four minutes ago. Chain of Life." END ON THE COUNTER.
sharpened.biggest_risk: The live end-to-end transport, not the algorithm. The DFS is 50 lines and the byLLM calls are individually trivial; what can eat the whole afternoon is the frontend -> jac-start REST (with its register/login token dance) -> byLLM -> graph JSON -> cytoscape animation loop being flaky on stage, compounded by live Gemini latency mid-demo. Secondary expression of the same risk: an unseeded random dataset in which the 6-chain, the P12 conflict, or the rescue path simply doesn't exist during the demo. Both are mitigated structurally — the 1:30-2:30 all-hands integration milestone with a hard 45-minute bailout to the snapshot-stepper transport, the hand-seeded dataset with an assert walker run before every rehearsal, and cached LLM responses behind an 8-second timeout for the exact demo inputs.
sharpened.fallback: Ordered cut list, invoked at the 3:30pm gate or the moment any dress run fails, per the judges' explicit warning. (1) Drop live REST first, not features: run every walker via `jac run` dumping phase-1..5 state JSONs, and the frontend becomes a stepper that plays the pre-computed snapshots — visually identical on stage, all computation still genuinely done by Jac walkers, immune to network and latency. (2) Cut the advocate-vs-arbiter subplot: keep one pre-generated ruling card as a static screen (15 seconds of demo) or delete the beat entirely; the spine of intake -> chain -> dropout-rescue -> counter carries all four judging criteria on its own. (3) Shrink the world: 4 hospitals to 2, 30 pairs to 14, 6-hop chain to 4-hop — the animation reads the same. (4) If byLLM misbehaves live, every LLM call falls through to a cached synthetic response for the exact demo inputs (built at 11:15, not at 6pm). Never cut, under any circumstances: the hop-by-hop chain animation, the dropout-rescue replan, and the lives-saved counter — those three ARE the project.
